To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook (Wattlebridge Holdings)

## Preliminary notes

- **Unauthorised fallbacks.** The Seller's draft adopts our two authority-gated fallbacks: the 20% cap and the 18-month claims period. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for either. We should therefore treat both as unagreed. Nothing in this draft should be read as triggering them.
- **Hidden fraud override.** The draft has no express fraud provision. Its "all Claims of any nature" language in cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, read with cl 12.3/13, would in effect extend the limitations to fraud. We should treat this as a substantive change, not a drafting point.
- **Seller's framing.** The cover email calls the package "fair and balanced." That is advocacy, not agreement. Several items in the Seller Update contradict the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, as noted below.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap

- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000). The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. No such authority has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** The Seller has pre-empted our fallback, and we have no authority to concede it.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket

- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, recoverable only on the excess (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure removes recovery of the first AUD 250,000.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit

- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. It also proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence.**
- **Reason:** This is a second unauthorised fallback, and the default-extension sentence would silently pull Title, Fraud and indemnities into the general regime.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime

- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, for "administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years; and
  - carve-outs from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty limitation clause.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we actually acquire what we pay AUD 24m for, so a 20% cap with 18 months is inappropriate.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out

- **Seller:** No express carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which on their face capture fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps;
  - baskets;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy; and
  - non-reliance.

  This position is non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an overriding fraud carve-out clause, and qualify cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 expressly by reference to it.**
- **Reason:** Our playbook does not permit this to be traded. The Seller's drafting achieves a fraud limitation by omission.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope

- **Seller:** Deemed general disclosure of:
  - the entire data room as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026 (DL 1.1); and
  - the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with no deemed disclosure of the data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Accept only the specific disclosures in DL 2 to 10, and only to the extent they are fair and specific. Also resist DL 1.4 to the extent it is used to dilute the effect of those disclosures.**
- **Reason:** General disclosure would neutralise the warranties against everything in the data room, including the very issues flagged below.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier

- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. If any qualifier survives, it should:
  - apply only to the actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; and
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3 in full.**
- **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, it would bar claims for the matters we have specifically identified and are seeking protection on.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent

- **Seller:** "Addressed," but on a reasonable endeavours basis only. The condition would be satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 2):** No final written consent exists, and there is no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - an effective consent, plus evidence that its cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Condition Precedent before Completion;
  - no consent-on-delivery mechanism; and
  - more than reasonable endeavours.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent, with evidence that its conditions are satisfied, a non-waivable-by-Seller CP. Require a stronger efforts standard and a Buyer walk right.**
- **Reason:** A material customer at around 30% of revenue is at risk, and the Seller's own letter confirms the issue is not "addressed."

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility

- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 3):** The facility is not repaid and no discharge exists. The facility also contains a change-control provision (cl 8.1).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds; and
  - executed security releases delivered at Completion.

  A post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require a payout letter, a direct payment line in the funds flow, and releases delivered at Completion.**
- **Reason:** Completing into a debt-free deal with live security and a change-control trigger would expose the Company. No approval exists for any post-Completion release alternative.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses

- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 5):** The bonuses are not in the funds flow, and the treatment of payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs is unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item (deducted or paid at Completion) or otherwise Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add an express funds-flow line and a Seller indemnity for the bonuses and on-costs.**
- **Reason:** The liability sits in the Company we are buying, and "a matter for the Seller" gives us no enforceable protection.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity

- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 4):** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. AUD 180,000 is shown as open, but this is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity covering ownership, title and use of the Ironquay deliverables, while preserving the SOW3 cure (payment and confirmatory assignment). The AUD 180,000 figure should not be treated as verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Broaden the indemnity to Ironquay IP ownership and infringement loss generally. Keep the SOW3 cure, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable.**
- **Reason:** A payment-only indemnity does not cover the real risk that the Company does not own the materials.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)

- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 6):** About 1,240 records went to an unintended recipient. Access, scope and any notification duty are all unestablished.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - preservation of logs;
  - completion of the investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion; and
  - appropriate warranty or indemnity protection.

  We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Add pre-Completion covenants (preserve logs, investigate, update the Buyer, consult on any notification decision) and a specific indemnity. Make no assertion of breach or a numeric claim.**
- **Reason:** The facts are genuinely open, so we need protection and information rights, not conclusions from either side.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals

- **Seller:** The three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 8):** It does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of the renewals, with no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor counter yet. Raise DD requests on necessity, terms, termination rights, accrual and timing (DD-008 and DD-011 read together). Reserve the treatment.**
- **Reason:** The facts are insufficient to justify either the Seller's "ordinary course" label or a Buyer deduction.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller:** Limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), and to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5). Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Define each claim category, specify which limitations apply to each, and delete the catch-all language.**
- **Reason:** The default wording collapses every bespoke protection into the general cap and time bar.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification

- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 10):** DD-012 is identified as the source relied on, and the Seller notes it does not represent completed Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, freedom from encumbrances and authority, such as:
  - ASIC records;
  - PPSR searches;
  - share certificates;
  - historical transfer documents; and
  - board and shareholder authorities.

  The DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as sufficient. Require independent title deliverables, and back title with Fundamental Warranties (see SPA-N-004).**
- **Reason:** An internal register the Seller supplied cannot verify the Seller's own title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as OPEN. Neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution should be assumed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation, outside the general regime.**
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed, and the Seller cannot settle these terms by assertion.

---

## Suggested next steps

1. **Escalation.** Escalate nothing to Amelia Frost unless the team actually wants to consider using the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. If it does, any authority must be in writing and must identify this draft.
2. **Mark-up priorities.** Prioritise the following non-negotiables in the mark-up:
   - fraud carve-out (005);
   - Fundamental/Title regime (004);
   - deletion of general disclosure and the knowledge bar (006, 007);
   - category separation (014);
   - Bluefen CP (008); and
   - Riverlark payoff (009).
3. **DD requests.** Issue DD requests on Sandbar (013), DD-006 (012), Ironquay payment status (011) and bonus on-costs (010).

- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Broaden the indemnity to Ironquay IP ownership and infringement loss generally. Keep the SOW3 cure, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable.**
- **Reason:** A payment-only indemnity does not cover the real risk that the Company does not own the materials.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)

- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 6):** About 1,240 records went to an unintended recipient. Access, scope and any notification duty are all unestablished.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - preservation of logs;
  - completion of the investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion; and
  - appropriate warranty or indemnity protection.

  We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Add pre-Completion covenants (preserve logs, investigate, update the Buyer, consult on any notification decision) and a specific indemnity. Make no assertion of breach or a numeric claim.**
- **Reason:** The facts are genuinely open, so we need protection and information rights, not conclusions from either side.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals

- **Seller:** The three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 8):** It does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of the renewals, with no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor counter yet. Raise DD requests on necessity, terms, termination rights, accrual and timing (DD-008 and DD-011 read together). Reserve the treatment.**
- **Reason:** The facts are insufficient to justify either the Seller's "ordinary course" label or a Buyer deduction.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller:** Limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), and to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5). Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Define each claim category, specify which limitations apply to each, and delete the catch-all language.**
- **Reason:** The default wording collapses every bespoke protection into the general cap and time bar.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification

- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Seller's own disclosure (DL 10):** DD-012 is identified as the source relied on, and the Seller notes it does not represent completed Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, freedom from encumbrances and authority, such as:
  - ASIC records;
  - PPSR searches;
  - share certificates;
  - historical transfer documents; and
  - board and shareholder authorities.

  The DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as sufficient. Require independent title deliverables, and back title with Fundamental Warranties (see SPA-N-004).**
- **Reason:** An internal register the Seller supplied cannot verify the Seller's own title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as OPEN. Neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution should be assumed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation, outside the general regime.**
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed, and the Seller cannot settle these terms by assertion.
